>Yes, and you don't need to remove private property for everyone to fight that problem.

Part of the problem you're encountering here is that socialism, even communism, doesn't necessarily do away with the idea of "private property". Nobody is coming for your toothbrush, let alone your iphone. Your photo album is not communal property to the state. 

Private property and capital ownership are [CARDINAL] very different fundamental things. 

Think of it this way: there are some things that are declared national resources and are monitored by the government. Technically your not, for example, allowed to move large amounts of gold out of the country without the government knowing about it.

Consider factories or lines of assembly as national resources. Since their existence matters to us nationally and communally, we get a say in what they do. This can take a large number of forms, from having workers on the board of directors by law, to democratic/planned decisions on what the factories will make, to co-ops where the workers \*own\* the means of production at that factory communally and as a co-op makes decisions about what to do. But the basic idea is to democratize capital resources so that other stakeholders get a say in how the business is run beyond the owner of the factory. 

What that factory makes can still be owned. Like I said, nobody is coming for your toothbrush.

>Would corruption disappear in a world where we truly govern democratically?

Not necessarily, and the problem with democratizing the workplace is that the goes outs is only as good as the goes ins. 

Look at unions for example. An educated, motivated, passionate union will be well run and offer not just a service to it's union members but arguably valuable services beyond just labor to the employers- You promise proficient, trained workers, you have a central point you can go to with complaints, the union in theory disciplines it's union members and keeps them professional and resolves issues if the members don't behave properly.

In a thriving, committed union, corruption is countered by the will of the many. There's just not enough corrupted numbers to overcome solidarity. 

But, and I've seen this [ORDINAL] hand, if you have most of the union members that are grudging members of the union, or apathetic, or have dropped out and don't attend meetings, or are uneducated/uninformed, then corrupt people can work their way into places of power and turn the system into cronyism. 

So the socialist answer is to educate the hell out of the youth, teach them that they're part of a whole and to care about each other, and empower them to make decisions and participate intelligently and with forethought, and to \*maintain\* that underlying infrastructure no matter what challenge to it you see.
